discussions.title: Download Hub: let your NAS do the downloading
discussions.body:
Paste a link and your NAS downloads it, even after you close the browser. Download Hub handles plain HTTP/HTTPS files, torrents (`.torrent` files and magnet links), ED2K links and videos from the sites yt-dlp supports. It runs on the official Gopeed engine.

What sets it apart is search: when a torrent site sits behind a Cloudflare check that the NAS can't get past, Download Hub lets **your own browser** open that page in a background tab and read the results back. So those sites still show up in your search.

![Browser-assisted search: sources behind Cloudflare show Needs browser](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f356a31-6da6-4b2d-89cf-5d2010ed4d2b)

## The big ideas

- **Almost any link.** HTTP/HTTPS, BitTorrent (`.torrent` files and magnet links), ED2K, plus videos from sites supported by yt-dlp.
- **Search that gets past Cloudflare.** With browser-assisted search, sources blocked by a Cloudflare check are searched through your browser instead of being skipped.
- **Everyone gets their own list.** Each DSM user has their own downloads, save folder and preferences.
- **Admins stay in control.** Admins choose who can use it, plus which extensions and engine updates go in. Updates are verified and can be rolled back.

## 1. Pick where files go

At the top of **Downloads**, **Save to** shows your folder. Click **Change** to pick another one. Files keep saving there in the background, even after you sign out.

![Downloads list](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55995e0f-5042-40de-b7a3-4ed1cbe00402)

## 2. Add a download

Click **New download** and paste one or more links, one per line. You can also use **Open file** for a `.torrent`. Download Hub sorts the links by type. For torrents you can tick **Choose files after adding** to pick which files you want.

![New download dialog](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ccaacd09-60a2-4aec-944c-13ec94f1c023)

Click **Add**. Pause, resume or filter downloads from the list, or use **Pause all** and **Resume all**.

## 3. Search instead of hunting for links

Open **Search**, type a name and pick a category and sources. The results come from all the sources you chose. Sort them, then click **Download** on the one you want.

![Search results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a911f57c-a235-497f-85c2-e4985604f3be)

Add your own sources (Torznab, RSS and more) under **Settings › Search sources**. If a source needs an account, a **Sign in** chip appears next to it: add the username and password (or a cookie) in Settings.

## 4. Turn on browser-assisted search (sites behind Cloudflare)

Some public torrent sites put a Cloudflare check in front of their pages. Your NAS can't pass it on its own, so those sources show **Needs browser** and a note says *Sites behind Cloudflare are skipped until browser assist is on*.

Browser-assisted search fixes that with the free **Remote Tab Opener** (RTO) browser extension:

1. **Install Remote Tab Opener** in the browser you use for Download Hub (the links for Chrome/Edge and Firefox are right on the Search page).
2. **Enable RTO** and reload Download Hub. The status chip changes to **RTO ready**.
3. **Allow the source domain.** The first time Download Hub opens a site, RTO asks for permission. Choose **Allow access to this domain**.

Now search as usual. Download Hub opens each blocked source in a background tab of your browser, reads the results and shows them next to everything else. While it works, the source shows **Waiting for browser**. If a site still wants you to finish a check, do it in that tab. If something goes wrong, click **Retry**.

![RTO ready: every source returns results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43030d66-0d25-4fc1-9f81-7785e3198cda)

Good to know:

- RTO only reads pages on the source domains you allow, and site cookies stay in your browser. They never go to the NAS.
- Magnet links come back directly. If a page only offers a `.torrent` file, save it yourself and use **New download › Torrent file**.
- Keep Download Hub open until the results come in. Downloads you've already added keep running on the NAS after you close the browser.
- It works on a computer. A phone browser can't run RTO, so on a phone those sources are left out.
- Browser assist is for getting past checks, not for logging in. Sources that need an account use the saved sign-in from **Settings › Search sources**.

## 5. Turn on video downloads (admins)

Video and audio downloads use **yt-dlp**. Until it's installed, video links won't download. An admin installs it under **Core updates › Media tools**, along with FFmpeg (for best-quality merges) and Deno (needed for some YouTube formats). They come only from official GitHub stable releases.

![Core updates and media tools](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a139961-60aa-4ace-b09e-84d02c5d0e79)

On x86_64 NAS models you can also install **gallery-dl** for image galleries.

## Tips & FAQ

**Can I follow a channel?**
Yes. Under **Settings › Media**, follow a channel and Download Hub checks it every 6 hours by default. New uploads get queued as normal downloads. You can also set rules per site, like "save this site's videos into `Videos/YouTube`".

**Extensions?**
**Extensions** lets admins install Gopeed extensions from the official catalog or a GitHub URL. Extensions run in the shared engine and can see every user's download links, so only install ones you trust.

![Extensions](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca6e60f2-e69f-45fe-882b-fed380519dc6)

**Torrents are slow.**
Allow the BT listening port (default `16889`) for both TCP and UDP in the DSM firewall and on your router. The same goes for the ED2K ports if you use them. You'll find them in **Settings › General**. That's also where you set seeding limits and how many downloads run at once.

![Settings](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/87a5d534-8bcd-4a41-aebc-8436428aa8d5)

**My torrent finished but the file isn't in my folder yet.**
While a torrent is seeding, the file stays in a private staging area. It moves to your folder once seeding stops. Set **Stop seeding at share ratio** or **Stop seeding after** to keep seeding short. With both at 0, files save as soon as the download completes.

**Who can use it?**
Anyone you allow in DSM's **Application Privileges**. Admins manage the engine, extensions and media tools.

**Which NAS models?** x86_64 and aarch64.

---

[Get Download Hub](https://synopkgland.com/apps/SynoPkgGopeed/) · [Browse packages](https://synopkgland.com/apps/)

discussions.title: Syno Connect Center: reach your NAS from anywhere, no port forwarding
discussions.body:
Syno Connect Center shows you, on one screen, every way your NAS can be reached from outside. If DSM's own **QuickConnect** or **DDNS** is turned on, it's listed too, for reference. Need another way in? Set up Cloudflare, Tailscale, NetBird or IPv6 direct right there in a few clicks, with no port forwarding. DSM sign-in stays on by default.

![Overview: Cloudflare and Tailscale set up here, QuickConnect and DDNS from DSM](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f14012a-c81d-42f9-b66d-d5aee3188d73)

## The big ideas

- **Everything in one place.** Every way in gets its own line on **Overview**, with its address, a QR code and whether it's running. QuickConnect and DDNS are read from DSM and shown as they are; you still change them in DSM's Control Panel.
- **No open router ports.** Cloudflare links run through a tunnel, and Tailscale and NetBird use a private network.
- **Pick one way, or mix them.** A free workers.dev link, your own domain on Cloudflare, Tailscale (or Headscale), NetBird (including a self-hosted server) or IPv6 direct access. Each one works on its own.
- **You choose which apps are reachable.** Add Syno Package Land apps, native DSM apps or any web service on your NAS, one at a time.
- **DSM made for your phone.** Connect adds a phone version of DSM at `/m` on your NAS address. More on that below.

## 1. Start the setup wizard

On first launch, **Overview** shows your NAS on the local network. Click **Set up**.

![First visit: Set up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fa28baf-40d9-440c-95a5-e1d167fd63cc)

## 2. Choose how you want to connect

The wizard compares the three common choices side by side: cost, who can open it, what you need to install and whether video works well.

![Step 1: Choose how](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4e91a38-0cd7-408c-b367-685fa6c4cb2f)

Quick guide:

- **Free link** — free, no domain needed. Good for DSM and light web apps, but not for video or large files.
- **My own domain** — a lasting address on a domain you own, through Cloudflare.
- **Only my devices** — Tailscale. Only your own signed-in phones and computers can reach the NAS. Video works fine.

Just want to try it out? **Get a temporary address** gives you a short-lived link right away.

## 3. Connect it

For a Free link, click **Open Cloudflare with the permissions filled in**. Create the token in your Cloudflare account and paste it back here. Read and tick the safety note, then click **Check and connect**. The wizard moves on by itself once the link works.

![Step 2: Connect Free link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c19b4914-8f43-49a5-ae00-a8db41949d9f)

> Before you open DSM to the internet, turn on 2-step verification and auto block in DSM. The wizard asks you to confirm this.

Then choose which apps should be reachable and open their links.

## 4. Check the Overview

Each connection you've turned on gets its own line on **Overview**: green means it's reachable from outside and running on the NAS. Copy the address, open it or show a QR code.

![Overview with three connections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/747761df-e077-48d3-92e5-28e78ee21b25)

## 5. Manage your apps

**App URLs** lists every app, which connections open it and its address. Click **Add app** to add another web service. If something needs attention, the app's row says what and whether it will fix itself.

![App URLs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c85980f6-3723-402f-b484-4ddb58fd6886)

## 6. Use DSM on your phone (Mobile View)

This is the part people miss. Open the normal DSM in a phone browser and you get the desktop: tiny windows you have to pinch and zoom. With Connect installed, add `/m` to your NAS address (for example `https://mynas.quickconnect.to/m`) and you get a different page, built for phones.

![Mobile View: Home, Apps and Storage Manager](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ff3f9bd-0fd4-4398-b759-0d3c2c2bf0ea)

- **DSM Apps, laid out for phones.** Open Storage Manager, Control Panel, File Station and your other apps from the **Apps** tab. Pages and tables fit the screen, and wide tables scroll sideways with the first column pinned.
- **Same account, same permissions.** Sign in with your usual DSM account. Nothing new to set up.
- **Live status on the home page.** CPU, memory, network and drives update live. Anything that needs attention, like a Security Advisor warning, sits at the top.
- **Notifications.** All your DSM notifications in one list, filtered by errors, warnings and info.

![Mobile View: Security Advisor, live resources and notifications](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a879e4a-0c67-4deb-ac6c-f3c2e5da9cb8)

**How to open it:** click **Connect your phone** at the top of Overview (or scroll to **Use DSM on your phone**). Under **Connect through**, pick which way your phone should use: QuickConnect, DDNS, a Cloudflare link, Tailscale, NetBird, IPv6 or your local network. Then scan the QR code. The phone in the middle is a preview with demo data: tap it to try Security Advisor, resources and notifications.

![Use DSM on your phone: QR code, phone preview and Home Screen steps](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca9163d4-fcfd-4380-8304-5b15ae094c70)

A few things to know about the way you pick:

- **Tailscale or NetBird:** install that app on the phone and sign in first.
- **Local network:** only works on the same network as the NAS.
- **IPv6 direct:** the browser shows a certificate warning.
- **Temporary address:** it changes when the NAS or Connect restarts.

**Make it feel like an app:** add it to your Home Screen. On iPhone, open the link in Safari, tap **Share**, then **Add to Home Screen**. On Android, open it in Chrome, tap the ⋮ menu, then **Add to Home screen** or **Install app**. From then on it opens full screen, with its own icon.

## Tips & FAQ

**Can I limit who opens my own-domain links?**
Yes. Under **Cloudflare › Own domain › Who can access**, turn on **Restrict access by email**. Visitors then get a one-time code by email (Cloudflare Access, Zero Trust Free). This only covers your own domain, not Free links or temporary addresses. Native apps like Synology Photos or Drive can't pass the browser email check.

![Own domain: who can access](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10c75155-5cd7-4570-a724-0ab71f4f2c1c)

**Which way should I pick?**
Open **Overview › Compare all ways** for a full table, including QuickConnect and DDNS that are built into DSM. Using more than one connection doesn't make anything faster or add failover. Pick the one that fits.

**Does it need anything on my router?**
No, Cloudflare, Tailscale and NetBird don't. IPv6 direct is the exception: it needs IPv6 on your network, and the guide in the app walks you through it.

**Requirements:** DSM 7.2 or later. Sign in with a DSM administrator account.

---

[Get Syno Connect Center](https://synopkgland.com/apps/SynoPkgConnect/) · [Browse packages](https://synopkgland.com/apps/)

discussions.title: Syno Reclaim: find out what's eating your NAS space, and free it safely
discussions.body:
![Delete a 10 GB folder on Btrfs: you may only get 3 GB back](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09555c0d-3314-4c35-a333-655961933ec3)

Here's the Btrfs truth: deleting a file or folder doesn't always free its space. If a snapshot still holds the data, or a clone or reflink copy shares the same blocks, those blocks stay put until the last thing pointing to them is gone. So that "10 GB" folder might only give you 3 GB back. Syno Reclaim tells you how much you'd *actually* get back before you delete anything, then helps you clean up without nasty surprises.

## The big ideas

- **Real numbers, not file sizes.** In **Explore**, next to each folder's size you see **Can free**: how much deleting it really frees. It also notes what holds the rest, like a snapshot, a reflink copy or a hard link.
- **Duplicates, found from metadata.** On Btrfs volumes it finds identical folders and big duplicate files without reading your file contents.
- **Nothing is deleted for good.** Cleanups go to the shared folder's Recycle Bin, so you can restore anything you change your mind about.
- **It tells you what it can't clean.** Snapshots, package data and Recycle Bins each get their own page that explains where to free that space.

## 1. Run a scan and look at the Overview

Open Syno Reclaim and click **New scan**. When it's done, **Overview** breaks the volume down **By type**, **By shared folder** or by **Packages**.

![Overview: where the space went](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5c76320-12d7-4abe-a5d9-3b2e44f71b80)

> Some features need system tasks. If a page asks for them, approve them once in **Settings › System access**.

## 2. Find duplicates

Go to **Duplicates** and pick a shared folder. **Identical folders** lists whole folders that exist more than once. Next to each one you can see which copy is kept and how much removing the others frees.

![Identical folders in a shared folder](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca033fdd-4e39-4323-b13b-fcbd55ea6473)

Switch to **Big duplicate files** to catch large files (10 MB or more) stored more than once. Filter by **Photos**, **Videos** or **Music** if you want.

![Big duplicate files](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3cad42f7-cae8-4c5a-a5f7-2ce6648746b1)

Tick what you want gone, or use **Select all duplicates in …** to take everything in that folder at once.

## 3. Review, then clean up

Click **Review and clean up**. The confirm dialog lists every item, how much moves to the Recycle Bin and how much you'll free once the bin is emptied. Tick the checkbox and confirm.

![Confirm cleanup dialog](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b569f035-cc30-4e6c-a7e9-0cc672e954a7)

The plan is checked again right before it runs, so if something changed since the scan, Reclaim won't touch it.

## 4. Empty the Recycle Bin when you're sure

Reclaim never empties a Recycle Bin for you. The **Recycle Bin** page shows how much each shared folder's bin holds and how much emptying it frees.

![Recycle Bin page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3271a37d-c690-40ee-92d8-b46aea8b91fb)

Empty the bin in DSM: **Control Panel › Shared Folder › Action › Empty Recycle Bin**. Want it automatic? Use a Recycle Bin task in Task Scheduler.

## Tips & FAQ

**"I deleted a lot but free space barely moved."**
Snapshots are probably holding the data. Open **Snapshot**, pick the shared folder and select snapshots. Reclaim calculates exactly how much deleting them would free. Then click **Delete in Snapshot Replication** to do it there. Reclaim itself never deletes snapshots.

![Snapshot page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b74a0ec-6204-4169-bfdf-0f81c3585b6c)

**What about package data, like Synology Drive or Container Manager?**
The **Packages** page shows how much each package uses and how to free space in that package. For example, it tells you which stopped containers and unused images to remove in Container Manager. Reclaim never deletes package data.

![Packages page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/93d8dbbd-fd61-410c-b046-c2a3c49d5855)

**Which copy of a duplicate is kept?**
Each group keeps one copy. Reclaim prefers a copy in one of your preferred shares. Without one, it keeps the oldest copy. To always keep copies in a certain share (say, `photo`), add it under **Settings › Preferred shares for kept copies**. You can also open a group to change which copy stays, or untick a copy to keep it too.

**Does it work on ext4?**
Space analysis and cleanup work on Btrfs and ext4. Duplicate finding needs Btrfs.

**Who can use it?**
DSM administrators only.

---

[Get Syno Reclaim](https://synopkgland.com/apps/SynoReclaim/) · [Browse packages](https://synopkgland.com/apps/)

discussions.title: Built-in web terminal in DSM, so you don’t have to open SSH
discussions.body:
It would be very useful to have a native terminal app inside DSM, accessible from the main menu like any other package.

Sometimes you just need to run a few commands, like checking a service, reading a log or fixing a permission. Today the only way is to enable SSH, connect from an external client, and then remember to disable it again. Opening the SSH port, even for a short time, adds an unnecessary attack surface.

A web-based terminal running inside the DSM session would solve this:

No SSH port to open: everything goes through the existing DSM web session (HTTPS).
Same user, same privileges: the shell runs as the user logged into DSM, with exactly the same rights. No privilege escalation, and sudo only for accounts that are already allowed to use it.
Admin control: access can be granted or denied per user or group through the standard DSM application permissions.
Traceability: sessions and commands can be logged in the DSM Log Center.

This would make day-to-day maintenance faster and more secure, especially for users who manage their NAS remotely and don’t want to expose SSH at all.

discussions.title: Connect 0.1.0-0052
discussions.body:
<!-- synopkgland:release:synopackageland%2FSynoPkgConnect:0.1.0-0052 -->

Connect **0.1.0-0052**

0.1.0-0052
- One overview page lists every connection method. Turn Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale, NetBird or IPv6 direct access on or off independently, or turn them all off.
- Cloudflare Tunnel: a temporary URL with no account, your own domain after signing in to Cloudflare (an existing DNS record is never overwritten), or your own tunnel token. Only the DSM web page is published.
- Tailscale: reach selected NAS web services from your own computers and phones; Funnel can make selected web services public.
- NetBird: sign in with your NetBird account, or use a setup key and your own management server in Advanced. Access to the NAS follows your management server's policy.
- IPv6 direct: use the NAS's global IPv6 address with checklists for the DSM firewall, router and DDNS. Connect does not change the firewall or your router.
- The cloudflared, Tailscale and NetBird clients are the vendors' official releases, downloaded and verified on the NAS before use.
- Only DSM administrators (local, AD or LDAP, as resolved by DSM) can open Connect and call its API. Everything runs as the package account, with no root helper.
- Nine languages; DSM 7.1 or later on x86_64, aarch64 and armv7.
- Fixed since 0.1.0-0047: starting and then stopping Tailscale or IPv6 direct no longer clears their saved services; NetBird failures show one clear message, and copying the NetBird IP works over http; Settings names GitHub's rate limit and when to retry, and says it is checking while a check runs; a page DSM gave no sign-in token asks you to sign in to DSM again.
- Upgrading from 0.1.0-0047 needs no administrator approval.
